title: Cheesy Stuffed Shells
subtitle: jumbo pasta shells filled with ricotta, mozzarella and Parmesan, baked in marinara under a blanket of melted cheese
imageAlt: Baked jumbo pasta shells stuffed with ricotta in red sauce with melted mozzarella in a baking dish on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 9×13 pan: dinner for two, plus 4 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Cook a few extra shells: some always tear. You need 24 good ones.

steps.title: Cook the shells
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Boil the shells in a big pot of water with the salt for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain, rinse with cool water and lay them apart on a tray so they don't stick.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Stir the ricotta, 1½ cups mozzarella, Parmesan, egg, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper together.

steps.title: Sauce the dish
steps.text: Spread 1 cup of the marinara over the bottom of a 23×33 cm (9×13 in) baking dish.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Fill 24 shells with a heaping tablespoon of filling each and set them open side up in rows in the dish.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Spoon the rest of the marinara over and around the shells and scatter the remaining 1 cup mozzarella on top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more, until bubbling, the cheese is golden and the centre reads 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes so the filling sets before serving.

fixIt.fix: Undercook them by 2 minutes and stir gently; they finish softening in the oven.
Drain watery ricotta in a sieve 10 minutes, and keep the egg in; it sets the filling.

fixIt.problem: Top browning before the middle is hot
fixIt.fix: Keep the foil on longer and check the centre with a thermometer.

saleTip: Ricotta and mozzarella often go on sale together at No Frills; shredded mozzarella freezes well.
swap: Add 450 g lean ground beef, browned to 71°C (160°F), to the marinara for a meaty version.
leftovers: Shells reheat beautifully; pack 4 per lunch container with extra sauce.
doneness: Bake until the centre reads 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, egg dishes and leftovers).
source: Based on tested baked stuffed shells methods (Canadian Living, Food Network Canada): par-cooked jumbo shells, ricotta-mozzarella-Parmesan filling bound with egg, baked covered then uncovered in marinara.
prepAhead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and chill; add 10 minutes to the covered bake.
Freeze assembled and unbaked up to 3 months; thaw overnight before baking.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2–3 minutes, or covered at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Ricotta and mozzarella filling with garlic powder, salt and pepper.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the Italian seasoning and Parmesan.

fancy.note: Garlic bread on the side and extra Parmesan on top.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: scatter the extra Parmesan over the mozzarella.

addSteps.title: Garlic bread
addSteps.text: Split the baguette, spread with the butter mashed with the garlic and bake cut side up for the last 10 minutes beside the shells.

plating: 3 or 4 shells per plate, sauce spooned over.

why.1-3: The egg sets the ricotta so the filling holds its shape when you cut in.
why.0-0: Undercooked shells soak up sauce in the oven instead of going mushy.
why.2-1: A covered bake melts everything; uncovering at the end browns the top.

funFact: Jumbo shells are 'conchiglioni' in Italian, from 'conchiglia', seashell.
